sections.title: Gambaran Anatomik SSP

content.text: The central nervous system consists of the brain and spinal cord. The brain is divided into cerebrum (two cerebral hemispheres), cerebellum, and brainstem (midbrain, pons, medulla oblongata). Understanding the anatomical relationships and vascular territories is essential for clinical localization.
Otak: serebrum, serebelum, batang otak
Sumsum tulang belakang
Sistem saraf tepi

sections.title: Suplai Darah Otak

content.text: ANTERIOR CEREBRAL ARTERY (ACA): Supplies medial frontal and parietal lobes, anterior corpus callosum, anterior limb of internal capsule, anterior fornix. Clinical deficit: contralateral leg weakness and sensory loss, abulia, urinary incontinence. MIDDLE CEREBRAL ARTERY (MCA): Supplies lateral frontal, parietal, and temporal lobes, posterior limb of internal capsule, basal ganglia. Clinical deficit: contralateral face/arm weakness and sensory loss > leg, aphasia (dominant hemisphere), neglect (non-dominant hemisphere), hemianopia. POSTERIOR CEREBRAL ARTERY (PCA): Supplies occipital lobe, medial temporal lobe, thalamus, midbrain. Clinical deficit: homonymous hemianopia, memory deficits, alexia without agraphia (dominant hemisphere).
ACA = leg weakness; MCA = face/arm weakness; PCA = visual field defect

sections.title: Kapsul Interna dan Suplai Vaskular

content.text: The internal capsule is a white matter structure containing ascending and descending fiber tracts between the thalamus/caudate and lentiform nucleus. ANTERIOR LIMB: frontopontine fibers, thalamocortical fibers. GENU: corticobulbar fibers (face). POSTERIOR LIMB: corticospinal tract (face, arm, leg in somatotopic order), thalamocortical fibers. RETROLENTICULAR: optic radiations, corticopontine fibers. SUBLENTICULAR: auditory radiations. Vascular supply: lenticulostriate arteries (branches of MCA) supply most of internal capsule. LACUNAR INFARCTS commonly affect the internal capsule, basal ganglia, thalamus, and pons. Pure motor hemiparesis from internal capsule lacune is the most common lacunar syndrome.
Lengan anterior: serat frontopontin, talamokortikal
Genu: serat kortikobulbar (wajah)
Lengan posterior: traktus kortikospinal (wajah, lengan, kaki), talamokortikal
Retrolentikular: radiasi optik
Sublentikular: radiasi auditorik
Suplai: arteri lentikulostriata (cabang MCA)
Internal capsule lacune causes pure motor hemiparesis - face, arm, and leg equally affected

sections.title: Analisis Gait

content.text: PARKINSONIAN GAIT: Shuffling steps, narrow base, flexed posture (stooped), reduced or absent arm swing, en bloc turning, festination (acceleration), difficulty initiating movement. HEMIPLEGIC GAIT: Circumduction of affected leg (swinging leg outward in arc), foot drop with toe dragging, extended knee on affected side, decreased weight bearing on affected leg, compensatory leaning. ATAXIC GAIT (Cerebellar): Wide-based, unsteady, veering toward affected side, positive Romberg. SPASTIC GAIT: Scissoring (adduction of legs), toe walking. STEPPAGE GAIT: From foot drop, excessive hip/knee flexion to clear foot. WADDLING GAIT: Bilateral hip girdle weakness, excessive trunk sway.

sections.title: Pleksus Brakhialis

content.text: The brachial plexus is formed by C5-T1 nerve roots, divided into roots, trunks, divisions, cords, and terminal branches. UPPER TRUNK (C5-C6): injury causes Erb-Duchenne palsy - 'waiter's tip' deformity (adducted shoulder, internally rotated arm, extended elbow, flexed wrist). Common in birth injury (shoulder dystocia) and motorcycle accidents. LOWER TRUNK (C8-T1): injury causes Klumpke palsy - claw hand deformity, weakness of intrinsic hand muscles, possible Horner syndrome (if sympathetic chain involved). LONG THORACIC NERVE (C5-C7): innervates serratus anterior; injury causes winged scapula.
Upper trunk (C5-C6): Erb-Duchenne palsy - waiter's tip deformity
Lower trunk (C8-T1): Klumpke palsy - claw hand, Horner syndrome
Long thoracic nerve: winged scapula
Erb-Duchenne (C5-C6): shoulder adduction, internal rotation, elbow extension; Klumpke (C8-T1): claw hand, intrinsic hand muscle weakness
